saints.name: Seraphim of Sarov
saints.sourceTitle: Repose of Venerable Seraphim, Wonderworker of Sarov

summary.text: Seraphim is remembered as a monk and elder of Sarov. The life begins with his childhood as Prochorus in Kursk and follows his monastic formation, solitary life, and ministry to visitors. It recounts his repose while at prayer in 1833. Accounts of visions, healing, and spiritual counsel remain attributed to the published life rather than newly composed by the app.

blocks.text: Seraphim’s secular name was Prochorus Moshnin. He came from Kursk, where his father was associated with building a cathedral and his widowed mother raised him. He entered Sarov as a young man, later received the monastic name Seraphim, and was ordained.

blocks.text: He lived for years in a forest hut near Sarov. The church history reports that robbers severely beat him and later repented after he forgave them. In 1810 he returned to the monastery in obedience to the abbot. In 1825 he opened his enclosure to visitors, later receiving pilgrims at the Near Hermitage.

blocks.text: Lopukhin’s historical address distinguishes the long preparation in solitude from Seraphim’s later work as an elder receiving people. He describes entry at Sarov in 1778, successive stages of monastic service and seclusion, and finally the opening of his cell to visitors. Lopukhin delivered this interpretation of his life in Belgrade in 1933.

blocks.text: The Sarov account says that he was found kneeling before an icon on January 2, 1833, after smoke was noticed in his cell. His death followed many years after the assault by robbers.
